title: Not one of the 10,158 tests bounds execution time or input size, so the entire ReDoS and unbounded-read class that AUDIT-012 found (one critical, four highs) is structurally uncatchable by this suite
category: bug class the suite cannot express
description: Scope: the whole tests/ tree. `performance.now` and `hrtime` appear zero times across all 356 test files. The only three `toBeLessThan(<3+ digits>)` assertions in the suite are about an array index (tests/app/api/v3/account/delete/route.test.ts:203), a string length (tests/lib/ai/scan-summary.test.ts:396), and a check count (tests/lib/scanner/checks-data/_schema.test.ts:238). No test feeds a large or adversarial input into a scanner detector and asserts a wall-clock budget, and no test asserts a body-size cap. That is precisely the shape of AUDIT-012#inj-01 (CRITICAL: maskPlaceholderSecrets runs a quadratic regex over a 1 MB body once per each of 74 detectors, reachable unauthenticated via /api/v3/demo-scan), AUDIT-012#inj-02 (a scanned site's robots.txt drives 9 seconds of backtracking in matchesRobotsRule), AUDIT-012#inj-03 (five detectors still run unbounded quadratic regexes over the full 1 MB body), AUDIT-012#ssrf-01 (safeFetch detaches every abort signal once headers arrive, leaving the body read with no time or size limit), and AUDIT-012#perf-02 (the source-map follow-up fetch has no body-read timeout). Every one of those files has high line coverage: lib/scanner/checks/content.ts and the secrets detectors are exercised in depth, just never with an input large enough or a clock assertion attached. This EXTENDS AUDIT-012#ssrf-09, which noted only that the safe-fetch suite skips the address-range block list; tests/lib/scanner/safe-fetch.test.ts (231 lines, 17 tests) also contains zero occurrences of maxBytes, size, byte, content-length, timeout, deadline, or abort.
impact: A single detector regex edited into a catastrophic-backtracking form, or a body-size guard removed, ships green. Because VulnRadar runs every scan in one Node process, one such input pins the event loop and the whole service stops answering, including for the ~50 paying accounts that had nothing to do with the scan. The suite gives false confidence here: coverage on these files is high, so a reviewer reasonably concludes they are well tested.
recommendation: Add tests/lib/scanner/_perf-budget.test.ts: build a 1 MB pathological body (a long run of word characters, plus a robots.txt with eight `*` wildcards for matchesRobotsRule), run each registered detector bundle and matchesRobotsRule against it, and assert Date.now() elapsed stays under a budget (500 ms per detector is generous and still catches a quadratic blowup). Separately, add cases to tests/lib/scanner/safe-fetch.test.ts that stream a body larger than the configured cap and assert the read aborts, and that a slow body stream is cut off by a deadline, mirroring the shape of AUDIT-012#ssrf-01.

title: No test asserts that a scan path charges the daily quota, which is why all four unmetered scan paths AUDIT-012 found pass the suite cleanly
category: quota accounting never asserted end to end
description: Scope: every scan entry point plus lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts. Eighteen test files reference daily-limits at all, and they are the paths that already charge correctly (scan/route, scan/bulk, scan/crawl, scan/authenticated, schedules, keys, teams, webhooks, browser/sessions). The four paths AUDIT-012 filed as unmetered are exactly the four whose tests never mention it. tests/app/api/v3/scan/discover/route.test.ts mocks six modules (db, auth, rate-limit, api-keys, safe-fetch, dns/promises) and neither of the quota modules, so AUDIT-012#abuse-01 (the two recon endpoints run outside the scan quota, ~200,000 DNS lookups and HTTP probes an hour from one free account) is invisible to it. tests/lib/scanner/scheduled-scans-worker.test.ts mocks nine modules (db, safe-fetch, engine, async-checks, execute-scan, plan-limits, notifications, email, runtime-config) and neither daily-limits nor concurrent-scans, so AUDIT-012#abuse-04 (scheduled scans run with no quota charge, no concurrency slot, and no access-rules check) is invisible to it. Same pattern for AUDIT-012#abuse-02 (API-key crawls skip the quota) and #abuse-03 (the AI chat context path has no token quota). The suite tests that the quota function works; it never tests that a given entry point calls it.
impact: Metering is the product's revenue control and its abuse control, and the suite cannot tell metered from unmetered. Four separate paths shipped free-scan capacity to anyone with an account, and none of them registered as a test failure. Any new scan entry point added tomorrow inherits the same blind spot, so this is a recurring cost, not a one-off.
recommendation: Write one shared table-driven suite, tests/app/api/v3/scan/_metering.test.ts, that enumerates every scan-initiating entry point (scan, scan/bulk, scan/crawl, scan/authenticated, scan/discover, scan/crawl/discover, the scheduled-scans worker, the GitHub review path) and, for each, mocks lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits and lib/rate-limiting/concurrent-scans and asserts checkAndRecordRequest (or the documented equivalent) is called exactly once before any outbound work, and that a denied quota short-circuits with no fetch. Make the table the single list a new entry point must be added to, so an unmetered path is a failing test rather than a future audit finding.

title: db:restore pipes the dump into psql without ON_ERROR_STOP, so a restore in which every statement failed still prints "Restore complete." and exits 0
description: runRestore spawns `psql [connArg]` with no `-v ON_ERROR_STOP=1`, no `--single-transaction`, and no `-q`. psql defaults ON_ERROR_STOP to off, so it prints each statement's error to stderr, continues with the next statement, and exits 0 as long as it consumed its input. The only failure check is `if (exitCode !== 0) throw` at line 108, which therefore never fires for SQL errors. backup-db.mjs produces the dump with `pg_dump --no-owner --no-privileges --format=plain` (line 219), which contains no DROP statements and no CREATE DATABASE, so restoring into the DATABASE_URL the app has already booted against means every CREATE TABLE fails with "relation already exists" and every COPY into a table with existing rows fails on the primary key. All of those are non-fatal to psql. The script then reaches line 112 and prints "Restore complete." This is a different script and a different mechanism from AUDIT-012#obs-02 (which covers the scheduled backup job reporting success on failure); the backup artifact itself is correct here, plain-format pg_dump does capture schema, data and sequence setvals.
impact: The one command the project offers for disaster recovery cannot distinguish a complete restore from a total failure. The header comment tells operators to rehearse a restore against staging "before trusting it in a real incident", but the rehearsal will report success regardless of whether anything was actually restored, so the rehearsal proves nothing. In a real incident an operator will believe the database is recovered when it may contain none of the backed-up rows.
recommendation: In scripts/restore-db.mjs, spawn psql with `["-v", "ON_ERROR_STOP=1", "--single-transaction", connArg]` so the first error aborts with a non-zero exit and the whole restore rolls back rather than half-applying. Add a `--into-empty` preflight that counts public tables in the target and refuses to run when the target is non-empty unless an explicit `--force` is passed, and after a successful restore print the row counts of a few core tables so the operator has positive evidence.

title: The SSRF guard and the access-rule blocklist are stubbed permanently permissive in all three scan-route suites, so deleting both gates from the routes leaves the whole suite green
category: test would pass with the feature removed
description: Three route suites replace the two scan-target security gates with hard-coded always-allow stubs declared inline inside the vi.mock factory, so no test can override them and no test asserts they were even called. tests/app/api/v3/scan/route.test.ts:72 declares `validateScanTarget: vi.fn(async () => ({ safe: true }))` and :76 declares `checkAccessRules: vi.fn(async () => ({ allowed: true }))`. tests/app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.test.ts:68 and :75 do the same. tests/app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.test.ts:57 does it for checkAccessRules. A scripted scan of all 4,494 it/test blocks found zero occurrences of `safe: false` or a checkAccessRules `allowed: false` override in any of those three files, and zero `expect(validateScanTarget).toHaveBeenCalled` style assertions. The gates they stand in for are real: app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:276 calls validateScanTarget and returns 400 on !safe, :285 calls checkAccessRules and returns 403 on !allowed; app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:304 and :310 do the same; app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:341 does the checkAccessRules half. The exact mutation the suite does not catch: delete lines 275 to 295 of app/api/v3/scan/route.ts, lines 304 to 313 of app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts, and lines 340 to 352 of app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts, and every one of the 697 lines of scan/route.test.ts plus both sibling suites still pass. For contrast, tests/app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.test.ts:179 does drive `mockCheckAccessRules.mockResolvedValue({ allowed: false })`, which is the pattern the three scan routes are missing.
impact: The SSRF gate on the main scan endpoint is the control that stops a user pointing a scan at 169.254.169.254 or an internal 10.x host, and the access-rule gate is the operator blocklist for restricted infrastructure. Both have been fixed by prior audits (AUDIT-011 demo-scan SSRF, AUDIT-012 rebinding work). Right now a refactor that drops either call from any of the three routes, or that moves the call after the scan is already dispatched, ships with a fully green CI run. The failure is silent until someone scans a metadata endpoint through the product.
recommendation: In each of the three suites, replace the inline `vi.fn(async () => ({ safe: true }))` factories with module-scope handles (`const mockValidateScanTarget = vi.fn(); vi.mock("@/lib/scanner/safe-fetch", () => ({ validateScanTarget: (...a) => mockValidateScanTarget(...a) }))`) defaulted to safe in beforeEach, then add two tests per route: one driving `{ safe: false, reason: "..." }` and asserting 400 plus that the scan was never dispatched (`expect(mockExecuteScan).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`), and one driving `{ allowed: false }` and asserting 403 with statusCode BLOCKED. Also assert `expect(mockValidateScanTarget).toHaveBeenCalledWith(normalizedUrl)` on the happy path so the call itself cannot be deleted.

title: A scan in flight during any process restart is left stuck at 'running' forever, with no automatic recovery
description: Scan cancellation and the scan watchdog are purely in-memory and per-process (lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts's own header comment concedes this explicitly: 'a scan whose process dies mid-run is left at running with no in-process timer left to rescue it'). The watchdog is a plain setTimeout closure tied to execute-scan.ts's call stack, so it is lost on any restart, not just a crash -- including a routine `docker compose restart`/redeploy. instrumentation.ts's graceful-shutdown handler (SIGTERM/SIGINT) only closes the DB connection pool; it never marks in-flight scan_history rows as failed/interrupted. lib/database/cleanup.ts, which runs a periodic sweep for every other kind of stale row in this app, has no logic that resets stale 'running'/'pending' scan_history rows on startup. The only way to clear a stuck row is the manual DELETE /api/v3/scan/status/[id] cancel endpoint, which nothing calls automatically and which the History UI does not surface for a scan that wasn't started in the current browser session. Net effect: every deploy that lands while any scan is mid-flight leaves that scan permanently spinning in the user's dashboard/history with no error message and no self-heal. Evidence: lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts lines 12-16 (doc comment) and lines 121-129 (startWatchdog, in-memory setTimeout); instrumentation.ts lines 2965-2975 (gracefulShutdown only calls pool.end()); grep for "status IN ('pending', 'running')" / "status = 'running'" across lib and app shows only lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts touches these states -- no reaper anywhere else; app/api/v3/scan/status/[id]/route.ts DELETE handler is the only path that can clear a stuck row, and it requires the user to know to call it.
recommendation: NOT YET APPLIED -- reported for review. Recommendation: On boot (instrumentation.ts), sweep scan_history for rows still 'pending'/'running' with started_at older than the max scan timeout and flip them to 'failed' with a reason like 'Interrupted by server restart.' Optionally also attempt this in the SIGTERM handler before pool.end() so a graceful restart doesn't even create the window.

title: The compiled AI knowledge truncates 20 of 52 docs callouts mid-sentence at 300 characters and leaks 64 raw JSX `{" "}` tokens and 19 undecoded HTML entities
description: scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs:274 and :284 both apply `stripJsx(...).slice(0, 300)` to every DocsCallout body. Measured across app/docs/*/page.tsx, 52 callouts are extracted and 20 exceed 300 stripped characters, so they land in lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md cut mid-word: for example the API page's Scopes callout ends at "returns 403 naming" (docs-knowledge.md:997) and the CI/CD callout ends at "before ch" (:1009). The offending pages are app/docs/api (2), config (2), github (2), rate-limits (2), scheduled-scans (2), self-hosting (4), sharing (2), account-security, developers, teams and triage. stripJsx (:82-110) also never strips the JSX whitespace literal `{" "}` (64 occurrences survive into the output) and never decodes `'`, `{` or `}` (19 occurrences), so those consume part of the same 300-char budget.
impact: lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md is what the in-product AI assistant answers from. Twenty of the most important "be careful about this" notes reach it as unfinished sentences, so the assistant either invents the missing half or drops the caveat. The Scopes callout in particular loses the sentence that tells the user a 403 names the missing scope.
recommendation: Raise the cap in scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs:274/284 to at least 1200 characters (the longest real callout is 522), or truncate on a sentence boundary; and add `.replace(/\{\s*"\s*"\s*\}/g, " ")` plus `'`/`&#\d+;` decoding to stripJsx before the existing entity replacements.

title: Twenty-three distinct inline alert geometries across 53 files, with four radii, three border opacities and two off-scale background opacities, because there is no Alert primitive
category: one-off components / inline alerts (53 files across app/ and components/, no primitive in components/ui/)
description: components/ui/ has no alert.tsx. 53 files hand-roll the inline error banner. Extracting every className that pairs a destructive border with a destructive background and has padding and a radius gives 23 unique strings, including: `rounded-md border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10 px-3 py-2 text-sm text-destructive`, `rounded-lg border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10 px-3 py-2 ...`, `rounded-lg border border-destructive/25 bg-destructive/5 px-3.5 py-3 ...`, `rounded-lg border border-destructive/20 bg-destructive/5 px-3 py-2.5`, `flex items-start gap-3 p-4 rounded-xl border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10` (app/teams/page.tsx:518), `rounded-xl border border-destructive/25 bg-destructive/3 p-4 sm:p-5`, `p-4 rounded-2xl mb-5 bg-destructive/10 text-destructive` and `flex flex-col gap-3 rounded-lg border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/6 p-4`. Radius spans rounded-md, rounded-lg, rounded-xl and rounded-2xl; border opacity spans /20, /25 and /30; background spans /3, /5, /6 and /10; padding spans p-3, p-4, px-3 py-2, px-3 py-2.5, px-3.5 py-3 and px-4 py-3. bg-destructive/3 and bg-destructive/6 are not steps on Tailwind's opacity scale, so they are one-off arbitrary values. The success side has the same problem plus a second syntax split: `bg-[hsl(var(--success)/0.1)]` and `bg-[hsl(var(--success))]/10` both appear for the same colour, and the success banner exists at rounded-md and rounded-lg with px-3 py-2, px-3 py-2.5 and px-3.5 py-3. AUDIT-013#dup-14 filed the state-management half of this (50 components hand-roll a useState banner pair while a full Radix toast stack serves one consumer); this is the visual half and it stands whichever way that decision goes.
impact: Error and success feedback is the highest-stakes UI in the product because it appears when something has gone wrong, and it looks different on every screen it appears on. Nothing signals "this is the app telling you something" consistently. A designer changing the error treatment has to touch 53 files and will miss some, and the two off-scale opacities mean two of the banners are already a shade nobody chose deliberately.
recommendation: Add components/shared/inline-alert.tsx exporting `InlineAlert({ tone, title, children, onDismiss })` with tone in error | success | warning | info. One geometry: `flex items-start gap-2.5 rounded-lg border px-3.5 py-3 text-sm`. One tone table using the dsn-01 foreground tokens: error `border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10 text-[hsl(var(--destructive-text))]`, success `border-[hsl(var(--success))]/30 bg-[hsl(var(--success))]/10 text-[hsl(var(--success-text))]`, warning `border-[hsl(var(--warning))]/30 bg-[hsl(var(--warning))]/10 text-[hsl(var(--warning-text))]`, info `border-primary/25 bg-primary/5 text-foreground`. Include the leading lucide icon (AlertTriangle / Check / AlertTriangle / Info) and role="alert" so every call site gets the announcement free. Migrate in batches by directory, starting with components/profile (the setError/setSuccess tree at components/profile/types.ts already threads one pair everywhere, so it is the cheapest) and app/teams/page.tsx:518, app/profile/page.tsx:695, app/repos/page.tsx:333 and app/attack-surface/page.tsx:45. Standardise the token syntax on `bg-[hsl(var(--success))]/10` (Tailwind opacity modifier) rather than the two-syntax mix, and delete the bg-destructive/3 and bg-destructive/6 arbitrary values.

title: The CLI's default 300-second timeout is the single-scan budget, so `vulnradar scan --crawl` in CI exits 1 as 'Timed out' on a crawl the server still has 600 seconds left to finish
description: cli/lib.mjs:5-:14 declares DEFAULTS with `timeout: 300` and `crawl: false`. cli/vulnradar.mjs:64 turns that into `const deadline = Date.now() + opts.timeout * 1000` and the poll loop at :65-:85 gives up at the deadline, printing 'Timed out after 300s waiting for scan ${scanId}.' at :88-:90 and calling process.exit(1) at :91. Server-side, 300 is exactly CONFIG_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (lib/config/config-values.ts:544) for a single-URL scan, but a crawl runs under CONFIG_CRAWL_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 900 (:551), enforced by the crawl watchdog at lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:361-:364. The CLI passes --crawl through but never adjusts its own deadline, and neither cli/lib.mjs:130 ('Give up waiting for the scan (default 300)') nor app/docs/cli/page.tsx:135 and :154 warns that --crawl needs a larger --timeout.
impact: A CI job that runs `vulnradar scan --crawl` against a site of any size fails red on a scan that is still running and will complete successfully. The user sees a timeout error, the pipeline blocks the merge, and the scan quietly finishes and lands in history a few minutes later, which reads as the tool being unreliable rather than as a default being wrong.
recommendation: In cli/lib.mjs, make the effective default conditional on the crawl flag (300 for a single scan, 900 for --crawl) while still honouring an explicit --timeout, and say so in the --timeout help text at :130 and in app/docs/cli/page.tsx's flag table.

title: marketing/ is entirely gitignored, so 401 packages, a 270 MB downloaded Chromium and a local .env full of credentials sit inside the repo tree with zero supply-chain visibility
category: untracked dependency tree inside the repo
description: First, the question that sets the severity of everything else here: marketing/ is NOT built or deployed as part of the product. `.gitignore:74` ignores the whole `marketing/` directory, `git ls-files marketing` returns 0 files, and no workflow, `next.config`, `vercel.json`, `tsconfig.json` or root script references it (grep for "marketing" across `.github`, `next.config.*`, `vercel.json`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` returns nothing). It is a standalone Remotion asset-generation project run manually on the maintainer's machine. Its dependencies therefore carry no production risk. What they do carry is a blind spot. Because `marketing/package.json` and `marketing/package-lock.json` are untracked, Dependabot cannot see them (it needs a committed manifest), `npm audit` at the root never walks into them, and the CycloneDX SBOM built from the Docker image (`.github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:82`) excludes them. Measured on disk: `marketing/node_modules` is 648 MB across 401 lockfile entries, of which `node_modules/.remotion/chrome-headless-shell/win64/` is 270 MB, a Chromium headless-shell binary that @remotion/renderer downloads over the network on first render rather than at install, and `@remotion/compositor-win32-x64-msvc` is another 29 MB of native binary including a bundled `ffmpeg.exe`. That tree executes on a machine where `marketing/.env` (365 bytes, present on disk, correctly ignored) holds credentials, and `marketing/package.json:31` wires `npm run audio` to `node scripts/make-audio.mjs`, which is what consumes them. The tree is also drifting on its own: React 19.2.3 against the root's 19.2.8, @types/react 19.2.7 against 19.2.18, prettier 3.8.1 against 3.9.6, eslint 9.19.0 against the root's 10.9.0.
impact: Nobody is watching 401 packages plus two downloaded native binaries that run with full user privileges on the maintainer's workstation next to a credentials file. A malicious postinstall or a compromised Remotion transitive release would execute there and nothing in the repo's security automation would notice, because from git's point of view the directory does not exist. Separately, the project is unreproducible: no other contributor can restore the exact tree that rendered the shipped videos, since the lockfile is not in git.
recommendation: Decide which of the two this is. If marketing/ should stay private, move it out of the repo working tree entirely (a sibling directory or its own repo) so it is not silently inside a scanned checkout, and keep a lockfile under version control wherever it lands. If it should stay in place, narrow `.gitignore:74` from `marketing/` to `marketing/node_modules/`, `marketing/out/`, `marketing/.env`, and `marketing/public/` so that `marketing/package.json` and `marketing/package-lock.json` become tracked, then add a `directory: "/marketing"` block to `.github/dependabot.yml`. Either way, document that the 270 MB chrome-headless-shell arrives on first `remotion render`, not on `npm install`.

title: The only regression guard for the scanner's per-check error isolation never makes a check throw, and its sole assertion is .not.toThrow()
category: test would pass with the feature removed
description: tests/lib/scanner/engine.test.ts:72 is titled "does not let one throwing check take down the whole scan". Its body builds a pathological body string (`"<".repeat(5000) + "html".repeat(1000)`) and asserts exactly one thing: `expect(() => runSyncChecks(...)).not.toThrow()`. No detector in the run is made to throw: a grep for `throw new Error` in that file returns nothing, and no detector is stubbed or injected. The feature it is supposed to guard is the pair of per-check try/catch blocks in lib/scanner/engine.ts at lines 169 to 172 and 186 to 198 (the file's own comment at line 131 calls them "the per-check try/catch below"). The exact mutation the test does not catch: delete both try/catch wrappers in lib/scanner/engine.ts, and the test still passes, because none of the 800-plus registered detectors throws on that particular input. It also does not assert that findings are still produced, so a mutation that makes runSyncChecks return `{ findings: [] }` unconditionally also passes.
impact: The per-check try/catch is what stops one bad regex or one bad detector from aborting an entire scan. If it is removed or narrowed during a refactor, the suite says nothing, and the symptom in production is a scan that returns a 500 or an empty result for every user whose page happens to trip the throwing detector. The test also carries a documented flake: its own comment at lines 65 to 70 records that the default 5s timeout "has been observed to flake under a full parallel suite run", which is why it now runs with a 20s override, so a very expensive test is buying an assertion that cannot fail.
recommendation: In tests/lib/scanner/engine.test.ts, register a deliberately throwing detector (or vi.spyOn one entry of ALL_INLINE_DETECTORS to throw) and assert two things: that runSyncChecks still returns, and that the findings from the other categories are still present. Keep the pathological-input case as a separate, honestly named smoke test.

title: Nothing limits requests per TARGET, nothing verifies ownership for an ordinary scan, and a wildcard robots.txt Disallow is deliberately ignored
description: Every limiter in the codebase is keyed on the caller, never on the victim. Grepping `key: \`` across app/api shows the rate-limit keys are all `${userId}` or `${ip}` (plus two per-account keys for login/signup email); there is no `${hostname}`/`${rootDomain}` bucket anywhere, and lib/rate-limiting/ contains no target-side concept at all. Domain-ownership verification (isUrlOwnedByUser, lib/domains/scope.ts) is applied only when the request asks for active probes or a port scan (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:310-324); an ordinary scan, crawl, bulk scan or schedule against any domain the caller does not own is permitted. checkAccessRules is an operator-maintained blacklist consulted on 5 of the scan entry points and absent from the two discover endpoints and the scheduled worker (see abuse-01, abuse-04); there is no shipped blocklist of sensitive target classes (.gov, financial, the product's own infrastructure). The crawler's robots.txt handling is deliberately partial: lib/scanner/crawl-discovery.ts:243 requires `value && value !== "*" && uaLower.includes(value.toLowerCase())`, so a site's `User-agent: *` / `Disallow: /` has no effect and only a group naming VulnRadar specifically is honoured (:207-216 documents this as intentional); `crawl-delay` is matched at :253 purely to mark that a rule line was seen and is otherwise discarded. On volume: one single-URL scan sends roughly 40-60 requests to the target (checkExposedFiles alone is ~23, per the comment at lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:2724 and :2799, plus checkGraphQLIntrospection up to 4 and the other live-fetch checks), and a crawl multiplies that by the page count (25 free, up to 250 elite).
impact: VulnRadar will point itself at any third party on request, at a rate limited only by how many accounts the requester creates, and a site owner has no working way to opt out: the standard wildcard robots.txt directive is ignored by design, crawl-delay is discarded, and there is no abuse contact path enforced in-product. A coordinated set of free accounts converges on one victim with no server-side signal that anything unusual is happening, and every request originates from VulnRadar's IP, so the operator absorbs the abuse reports and the blocklisting.
recommendation: Add a per-target bucket to lib/rate-limiting/ keyed on the registrable domain (extractRootDomain from lib/scanner/root-domain.ts) and check it in every scan entry point alongside the existing per-user check, so total inbound-to-one-victim volume is bounded across all accounts. Ship a default access-rules seed covering .gov/.mil and the deployment's own hostnames. Honour `User-agent: *` Disallow rules and crawl-delay in lib/scanner/crawl-discovery.ts for unverified domains, keeping the current ignore-wildcard behaviour only for a domain the caller has verified via isUrlOwnedByUser.

title: No poller anywhere in the app pauses when the tab is hidden: there is not one visibilitychange or document.hidden reference in the codebase
description: Grepping visibilitychange and document.hidden across app/, components/ and lib/ returns zero matches. Every recurring timer therefore keeps firing in a backgrounded tab: components/shared/notification-center.tsx:314 and :344 (two polls of /api/v3/notifications/active and API.NOTIFICATIONS every 300,000 ms by default), app/dashboard/page.tsx:140 (scan status, 2,000 ms, up to 16 minutes), app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:327 (browser session logs at LOGS_POLL_MS) and :202 (a 1,000 ms clock tick), components/admin/features/backup-manager.tsx:106 (2,000 ms), components/admin/features/updater-manager.tsx:171 (2,000 ms), components/admin/features/queue-status-manager.tsx:65 (45,000 ms), components/scanner/subdomain-discovery.tsx:202. Browsers throttle setTimeout/setInterval in hidden tabs to roughly 1/minute after a delay, but they do not stop fetches that a still-scheduled timer issues, and the 45 s and 300 s pollers are already slower than the throttle floor so they run essentially unthrottled.
impact: Users who leave the dashboard, an admin panel, or any page with the notification bell open in a background tab keep issuing authenticated, database-backed requests indefinitely. For an operator this shows up as a persistent request floor proportional to open tabs rather than to active users, and it is the kind of load that only becomes visible after the user base grows.
recommendation: Add a shared hook, e.g. lib/hooks/use-visible-interval.ts, that wraps setInterval and clears/restarts on document visibilitychange, and use it at components/shared/notification-center.tsx:314 and :344, components/admin/features/queue-status-manager.tsx:65, components/admin/features/backup-manager.tsx:106 and components/admin/features/updater-manager.tsx:171. For the fast pollers that track a real job (dashboard scan status, browser session logs) keep them running but back the interval off while hidden rather than stopping outright.

title: Nineteen API capabilities exist with no UI control, each with a specific screen it belongs on
description: Verified by reading each handler. POST /api/v3/scan/import-spec (parses OpenAPI 3, Swagger 2 and Postman, returns targets) has no UI caller; API.SCAN_IMPORT_SPEC exists at lib/config/client-constants.ts:145 referenced only by the changelog - belongs on the bulk tab of components/scanner/scan-form.tsx. Authenticated crawl is unreachable: app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:216,300-337 accepts the same auth block, but app/dashboard/page.tsx:415-449 routes any request carrying auth to the single-page endpoint, so deep plus a login silently downgrades. PATCH /api/v3/teams/members (role change, with ceiling and self-demotion guards) has no caller; the only way to change a teammate's role is remove and re-invite - belongs on components/teams/team-members-list.tsx:160. PATCH /api/v3/account/discord (syncAvatar, syncName) unreachable while components/modals/discord-profile-modal.tsx:27-28 has exactly those checkboxes but POSTs OAuth query-string values to /api/v3/auth/update, so it only works in the seconds after connecting. Badge revoke (DELETE /api/v3/badge/site?scanId=N, sets revoked_at) has no caller, so a badge pasted into a public README cannot be killed - belongs under the ScopeToggle at components/badge/badge-preview.tsx:261. Support tickets cannot be reopened: the route permits it at app/api/v3/support-tickets/[id]/route.ts:321-328 but both UIs only send resolved and closed, and replying to a closed ticket 409s. The updater can only install the newest release (app/api/v3/admin/updater/apply/route.ts:94,120-123 accepts any targetVersion; components/admin/features/updater-manager.tsx:185 always sends status.latest) so there is no rollback or pin. /api/v3/health returns schema_version vs schema_required, missing_tables, latency and pool stats and has no consumer, so a self-hoster needing a migration has no in-app signal. Stripe setup is curl-only, and both routes gate on role !== ADMIN exactly (setup-products/route.ts:31, setup-webhook/route.ts:36) which locks out super_admin unlike every other admin route. Also: teamId on schedules and webhooks, webhook type pinning (both UI paths hardcode "auto"), GitHub repo scan branch/ref, per-finding feedback notes, browser session viewport and ttlSeconds (the latter hardcoded to 360 at scan-actions-menu.tsx:384, defeating the admin setting), security alerts limit/offset/severity/user_id (hardcoded to 100 so alert 101 is unreachable), admin AI-conversations userId filter, admin notification email tone (hardcoded "info"), history rescan dropping all original scan options, scan source 'scheduled' rendering as "Web", admin content and public directory page sizes, and markAllRead on the notification bell.
impact: Nineteen shipped backend capabilities that no user can reach. Several are not conveniences: badge revoke has no alternative, authenticated crawl silently does something other than what was asked, and the health endpoint is the only signal a self-hoster has that their schema is behind.
recommendation: Triage by user harm rather than effort. Highest first: authenticated crawl (silent wrong behaviour), badge revoke (no alternative exists), team member role change (workaround is destructive), support ticket reopen (dead end), health panel (self-host blocker). The rest are ordinary missing controls.

title: No push/proactive alerting on production incidents -- everything is pull-based
description: There is no external error-tracking or alerting SDK wired into the app (no Sentry/Datadog/etc. in package.json). The admin System > Error Logs panel (a genuinely good feature -- see the 'checked and fine' note) captures console.error calls into a searchable table, and /api/v3/health returns 503 on a dead DB, but both are pull: an operator only learns something is wrong by opening /admin or by having set up their own external uptime monitor against /api/v3/health, neither of which this repo configures. A dead scheduled-scans worker, a run of failed Stripe webhooks, or a DB outage at 3am produces rows in a table and a 503 response that nobody is watching until a customer complains. Evidence: package.json has no @sentry/*, datadog, or similar dependency; app/api/v3/admin/error-logs/route.ts is a GET/DELETE the admin has to visit -- nothing pushes its contents anywhere.
recommendation: NOT YET APPLIED -- reported for review. Recommendation: Wire the health endpoint into an external uptime monitor (even a free one) that pages someone on 503, and/or add a lightweight Sentry-style SDK for exception capture with alerting, since the in-app error log viewer is a good diagnostic tool but not an alerting system.

title: POST /api/v3/scan/feedback accepts a caller-supplied scanHistoryId with no ownership check, letting any user attach fabricated feedback to (and trigger a forced recompute + host_reputation cascade against) any scan in the system
description:
FeedbackSchema only validates that `scanHistoryId` is a positive integer (app/api/v3/scan/feedback/route.ts:10); the POST handler never verifies `scan_history.user_id === session.userId` for it before inserting into scan_finding_feedback (scan_history_id FK just needs to reference an existing row, per instrumentation.ts's `scan_history_id INTEGER REFERENCES scan_history(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`) and before calling `recomputeScanScore(scanHistoryId)` (line 64). This breaks the exact convention the codebase documents for itself elsewhere -- e.g. app/api/v3/webhooks/[id]/route.ts's own comment: 'Every other per-resource route in this codebase ... verifies ownership in the same UPDATE ... WHERE id = $n AND user_id = $n statement ... so a [resource] ID belonging to another user can never be [mutated]' -- a pattern this route does not follow for scanHistoryId.

Impact: any authenticated user (including free tier) can POST arbitrary {findingId, findingUrl, verdict, notes} tied to any other user's scan_history_id (IDs are small sequential integers, trivially enumerable), polluting the scan_finding_feedback table that idx_scan_finding_feedback_finding_id (finding_id, verdict) indexes for the admin 'Engine Feedback' false-positive-rate aggregation (CONFIG_ENGINE_FEEDBACK_NOISE_THRESHOLD_PERCENT). It also forces recomputeScanScore to run an UPDATE against another user's scan_history row and against host_reputation `WHERE source_scan_id = scanHistoryId` for a scan the caller doesn't own and never touched otherwise -- a write side-effect triggered purely by an unauthenticated-for-that-resource request parameter. Evidence: app/api/v3/scan/feedback/route.ts:7-13 (FeedbackSchema, scanHistoryId has no ownership tie), line 39-54 (INSERT uses scanHistoryId as-is, no ownership SELECT), line 63-65 (`if (scanHistoryId) { recomputeScanScore(scanHistoryId).catch(() => {}); }`); lib/scanner/recompute-scan-score.ts:58-112 (reads/writes scan_history and host_reputation by that raw id).
recommendation: NOT YET APPLIED -- reported for review. Recommendation: Before inserting or calling recomputeScanScore, verify the caller owns the scan (or has team access, matching the pattern in app/api/v3/history/[id]/share/route.ts): `SELECT user_id FROM scan_history WHERE id = $1 AND user_id = $2`, returning 400/404 if scanHistoryId is present but not owned by session.userId. If it's intentional that feedback can reference a scan the user doesn't own (e.g. a shared/public scan they're reviewing), explicitly document that trust decision and still avoid triggering the host_reputation-cascading recompute for a scan outside the caller's own history.

title: CSRF exemption `pathname.startsWith("/api/v3/webhooks/")` intended only for the Stripe webhook receiver also exempts the user's own session-authenticated webhook-edit endpoint
description:
middleware.ts's isExemptFromCsrf() exempts any path starting with `/api/v3/webhooks/` from the Origin/Referer CSRF check, with the stated rationale 'Exempt endpoints authenticate the caller some other way (signed payload, server-issued secret, etc.)' -- true for app/api/v3/webhooks/stripe/route.ts (verified via STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET), but the prefix match also matches app/api/v3/webhooks/[id]/route.ts's PATCH handler, which edits a webhook's url/name/type/active flag using ONLY the session cookie for authentication (no signature, no secondary secret) -- exactly the class of endpoint the CSRF check exists to protect. This violates the function's own documented invariant: 'Keep this list narrow -- every entry needs a clear non-CSRF trust boundary,' which is not true for /api/v3/webhooks/[id].

Current practical exploitability is reduced (not eliminated) by the session cookie's `sameSite: 'lax'` attribute (lib/auth/auth.ts:65): a cross-site fetch/XHR PATCH (the only way to reach this endpoint, since HTML forms cannot send PATCH) does not carry SameSite=Lax cookies today in a standards-compliant browser, so this is currently a redundant-layer failure rather than an immediately exploitable one -- but it is a real gap in the app's primary, documented CSRF defense, and would become directly exploitable if a future route is added under this prefix that's reachable via GET/POST top-level navigation, or in any user-agent context where SameSite enforcement is weaker than assumed. Evidence: middleware.ts:314-327 (`pathname.startsWith("/api/v3/webhooks/")` in isExemptFromCsrf); app/api/v3/webhooks/[id]/route.ts:23-32 (PATCH authenticates via getSession() / cookie only, matches the exempted prefix); app/api/v3/webhooks/stripe/route.ts:38-40 (the actual signature-verified endpoint the exemption was written for).
recommendation: NOT YET APPLIED -- reported for review. Recommendation: Narrow the exemption to the exact Stripe path: `pathname === "/api/v3/webhooks/stripe"` instead of a prefix match, so /api/v3/webhooks/[id] (and any future path under this prefix) goes through the normal Origin/Referer CSRF check like every other session-authenticated mutating route.

title: The docs-knowledge compiler's staleness warning can never fire, and its page scan misses any nested docs page
description: scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs:609 writes the output file, and :614-625 then compares `statSync(OUTPUT).mtimeMs` against the newest page.tsx mtime to warn when "docs were edited N days after this knowledge file". Because the stat runs after the write, knowledgeMtime is always the current time and newestPage is always in the past, so `daysStale` is always negative and the `> 30` branch is unreachable. Separately, listDocPages (:66-81) reads only the immediate children of app/docs, so app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx is silently skipped: the run compiles 19 of the 20 docs pages, and the generated extraction-summary table (lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md:2163-2181) lists 19 routes with no playground row.
impact: The guard that was written to catch exactly the drift this section audits for is dead code, and any future docs page nested one level deeper (the pattern app/docs/api/playground already established) is excluded from the AI assistant's knowledge with no warning.
recommendation: Move the mtime read in scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs to before the writeFileSync at :609, and make listDocPages (:66-81) walk app/docs recursively for page.tsx instead of reading one directory level.

title: The prebuild knowledge compilers drop a bad source with a warning and still exit 0, and their only staleness guard is mtime-based so it can never fire in CI or a Docker build
description: package.json's `prebuild` chains the four `scripts/compile-*-knowledge.mjs` scripts with `&&`, so a non-zero exit does fail `npm run build`. But each script only exits non-zero on total failure, never on partial failure. scripts/compile-legal-knowledge.mjs:269-272 warns "missing <path>, skipping" and `continue`s past a legal page that has moved, and only exits 1 if `totalSections === 0` across every page (lines 307-310). scripts/compile-checks-knowledge.mjs:143-147 warns and skips a checks-data JSON file that fails to parse or is not an array (`readJsonSafe` swallows the parse error at line 60). scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs:545-546 exits 1 only when zero docs pages are found. The CI drift gate at .github/workflows/ci.yml:80-82 regenerates from the same tree and diffs, so it produces the identical truncated file and passes; I verified separately that `git diff --exit-code --ignore-matching-lines='compiled from'` does correctly ignore the date line and still exits 1 on a real content change, so that gate works as intended for its actual purpose (an edited source with a stale committed output). The only in-script drift detector is mtime-based (scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs:614-623 and scripts/compile-checks-knowledge.mjs:295-306, both computing `daysStale > 30` from `statSync().mtimeMs`), and git does not record mtimes, so on any fresh clone (CI, the Docker build's `COPY . .`, a self-hoster's `git clone`) every file carries the checkout time and `daysStale` is approximately zero. That warning cannot fire in any environment that produces a shipped artifact, and it is a `console.warn` that would not fail the build even if it did.
impact: Renaming or breaking a single legal page or checks-data category silently shrinks the compiled AI knowledge, the build stays green, the CI drift gate stays green, and the assistant answers about retention policy or an entire check category from nothing. There is no signal anywhere.
recommendation: In scripts/compile-legal-knowledge.mjs replace the `continue` at line 271 with `process.exit(1)`, since PAGES is a fixed list and a missing entry is a bug. In scripts/compile-checks-knowledge.mjs make a non-array or unparseable checks-data file fatal. Add a floor assertion to each script (expected page count, expected minimum check count) so a silent shrink fails loudly. Delete the two dead mtime staleness blocks: ci.yml:80-82 already covers the case they were meant to catch.

title: Six CSS variables are defined and never read, and eight Tailwind colour utilities are wired to variables that are never defined, so bg-sidebar silently renders nothing
description: Records design-language.md A3 item 8 as an actionable finding, verified against the current tree. app/globals.css:211-213 defines --surface-1, --surface-2 and --surface-3 for the light theme and :256-258 repeats them for dark. No file in app/, components/ or lib/ reads them, and tailwind.config.mjs does not map them to a utility either, so they are unreachable by any means. Separately, tailwind.config.mjs:64-73 declares a full `sidebar` colour group (DEFAULT, foreground, primary, primary-foreground, accent, accent-foreground, border, ring) resolving to hsl(var(--sidebar-background)) and seven siblings. None of those eight variables is defined anywhere in app/globals.css or any other stylesheet, and no component uses bg-sidebar, text-sidebar-foreground or any of the group. So the utilities exist, autocomplete offers them, and each resolves to hsl() with an empty argument, which is an invalid colour the browser drops.
impact: Six dead declarations in the critical CSS. More costly is the sidebar group: a developer building the next sidebar reaches for bg-sidebar because Tailwind's IntelliSense lists it, gets a transparent element with no error in the console or the build, and has to work out why. The product already has two sidebars (/profile and /admin) that both hand-rolled bg-primary/10 instead, which is what that group was presumably added for.
recommendation: Delete --surface-1, --surface-2 and --surface-3 from both blocks in app/globals.css (:210-213 and :255-258). For the sidebar group, decide once: either delete tailwind.config.mjs:64-73 entirely, or define the eight variables in both :root and .dark and use them in the shared section-nav component proposed in dsn-10. Deleting is the smaller change and matches how the two existing sidebars are actually built; if it stays, the variables must be defined in the same commit so the utilities are never resolvable-but-empty.

title: public/og-image.png bakes "VulnRadar" and "vulnradar.dev" into the pixels of the social card, and no documentation mentions the script that regenerates it
description: lib/config/config-values.ts:226 exposes CONFIG_SEO_OG_IMAGE = "/og-image.png" as a configurable SEO value, and lib/config/registry.ts registers SEO_OG_IMAGE, SEO_OG_IMAGE_WIDTH and SEO_OG_IMAGE_HEIGHT as admin-editable. The file the path points at is fixed content: public/og-image.svg:43 draws the wordmark "VulnRadar" and :58 draws "vulnradar.dev", and public/og-image.png is the 110 KB rasterisation of it. The config comment at :222-225 names the regeneration step ("edit public/og-image.svg then run `node scripts/build-og-image.mjs`"), but that instruction appears nowhere a self-hoster reads: grepping app/docs/ and README.md for "og-image" or "build-og-image" returns nothing, and the branding section of app/docs/config/page.tsx does not mention it.
impact: A renamed fork that changes CONFIG_APP_NAME and CONFIG_APP_URL still shares a social card reading "VulnRadar / vulnradar.dev" on every Twitter, LinkedIn, Slack and Discord unfurl of their own domain, which is the single most visible piece of branding the product emits. The fix is a two-minute SVG edit plus one script, but it is only discoverable by reading a comment in config-values.ts. On the pinned-image Docker path the asset cannot be changed at all, since public/ is baked into the image.
recommendation: Add a short "Social card" bullet to the branding subsection of app/docs/config/page.tsx (near the CONFIG_LOGO_URL bullet at :238) and to the rebrand block in app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:140-155: edit public/og-image.svg, run `node scripts/build-og-image.mjs`, rebuild. Better, have scripts/build-og-image.mjs read APP_NAME and the APP_URL hostname from lib/config/config-values.ts and substitute them into the SVG's two text nodes at build time, so a rename regenerates the card automatically and the asset stops being a third hardcoded copy of the brand.

title: The CLI's default API base is a bare literal with no environment variable, unlike its own API token which has VULNRADAR_TOKEN
description: cli/lib.mjs:6 sets `apiBase: "https://vulnradar.dev/api/v3"` in DEFAULTS. parseArgs at :56-57 accepts `--api-base <url>`, and app/docs/cli/page.tsx:129-132 documents it as "API base URL, for a self-hosted instance", so the CLI is genuinely repointable, unlike the extension in hc-02. What is missing is the env form: the sibling value on the next line, :26, reads `apiKey: process.env.VULNRADAR_TOKEN || undefined`, and the docs at app/docs/cli/page.tsx:110-112 specifically tell CI users to prefer the environment variable over the flag. There is no VULNRADAR_API_BASE. app/docs/cli/page.tsx:131 also prints the literal "https://vulnradar.dev/api/v3" as the documented default rather than deriving it, so a self-hosted instance's own CLI docs page advertises the hosted origin.
impact: A self-hoster using the CLI in CI has to repeat `--api-base https://scanner.theirdomain.com/api/v3` on every invocation in every workflow file, while the token next to it comes from the environment. Forgetting it once sends a scan request, with their API key in the Authorization header, to vulnradar.dev, where the key is not valid: the key leaks to a third-party host in exchange for a 401. Low severity because the flag exists and the failure is loud, but the asymmetry with VULNRADAR_TOKEN is an easy trap.
recommendation: In cli/lib.mjs, change :6 to read `apiBase: process.env.VULNRADAR_API_BASE || "https://vulnradar.dev/api/v3"` so the flag still wins and the env is the CI-friendly default, and add the variable to the options table and the CI guidance in app/docs/cli/page.tsx:110-132. Add a line to cli/README.md as well. The docs table's "Default" cell at :131 can stay literal (it is accurate for an unmodified CLI) but should gain "or VULNRADAR_API_BASE".

title: Renaming a fork requires editing 221 literal "VulnRadar" strings in 54 files that APP_NAME does not cover, concentrated in the changelog, the SEO comparison pages and the extension
description: Scope of the measurement: a Node scan of app/, components/, lib/, extension/src/, cli/, public/ and .github/ over .ts, .tsx, .mjs, .json, .svg, .yml, .html and .css, with // and /* */ comments stripped first, counting the literal token "VulnRadar" outside the config layer's own definition. Result: 221 occurrences across 54 files. The distribution matters more than the total. lib/changelog/data.ts has 84 (historical release notes, correctly frozen, should never be templated). lib/seo/alternatives.ts has 23 (the competitor-comparison pages, prose that reads as first-person product claims). lib/config/registry.ts has 12 (help text). extension/src/ has 44 across 10 files, on top of the separate hardcoding in hc-02. app/docs/api/page.tsx has 8 (Python SDK sample code, `from vulnradar import VulnRadar`). The genuinely templated surfaces are in good shape by contrast: every scanner User-Agent derives from APP_NAME (lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:376, execute-crawl-scan.ts:149, async-checks.ts:2701, crawl-discovery.ts:31, cve-enrichment.ts:111, osv-lookup.ts:88, software-inventory.ts:839, lib/ai/verify-findings.ts:146, lib/admin/alert-webhook.ts:71), and all four report exporters use APP_NAME and APP_URL throughout (lib/reports/pdf-report.ts, markdown-report.ts, sarif-report.ts, compliance-report.ts).
impact: GPL-3.0 makes a rebranded fork a legitimate and expected use, and the product markets itself as self-hostable, so this is a real cost to quantify rather than a defect. The honest number is that APP_NAME covers the app chrome and the reports, and roughly 220 further edits cover everything else, of which maybe 60 are actually user-visible on a renamed instance (the SEO comparison pages, the API docs SDK samples, five OAuth error messages at app/api/v3/auth/oauth/[provider]/callback/route.ts:193, :215, :281, :493, :536, and the extension surface). The changelog's 84 should stay as they are. One value is a wire protocol and should not be renamed at all: lib/webhooks/delivery.ts:27 sets `SIGNATURE_HEADER = "X-VulnRadar-Signature"`, which every existing customer receiver parses.
recommendation: Do not attempt a blanket rename. Fix the three cheap clusters and document the rest. (1) The five OAuth error messages in app/api/v3/auth/oauth/[provider]/callback/route.ts should use APP_NAME, they are one-line template changes on user-facing error copy. (2) lib/seo/alternatives.ts should take the product name from APP_NAME in its shared VR answers block at :43 rather than repeating the literal 23 times. (3) The extension gets APP_NAME from VULNRADAR.appName in extension/src/lib/constants.ts:7 already; the 44 literals should use it. Then add a "Renaming a fork" subsection to app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx listing what APP_NAME does and does not cover, naming lib/changelog/data.ts and lib/webhooks/delivery.ts:27 as deliberately not renameable.

title: .dockerignore patterns are root-anchored, so nested .env files (marketing/.env exists in this tree), the .claude worktree copy, audits/ and databases/ all enter the build context for the documented local-build path
description: Static analysis. Docker matches .dockerignore patterns against the whole context-relative path using filepath.Match semantics, where * does not cross a /, and only ** crosses directories. So `.env`, `.env.*` and `.env*.local` at .dockerignore:4-6 exclude only root-level dotenv files, and `node_modules` at :1 excludes only the root node_modules. A directory listing of this working tree shows ./marketing/.env present, which is not matched by any pattern; .claude/ (which per the audit brief holds a full second checkout at .claude/worktrees/agent-ad8a7d09dcde23fcc/, including its own node_modules), audits/, databases/ (gitignored at .gitignore:12 and described there as holding real pre-migration database backups), and cli/ are not listed either. Dockerfile:27 is `COPY . .`, so all of that lands in the builder stage. It does NOT reach the published image: the runner stage copies only public, .next, node_modules, package.json and next.config.mjs (Dockerfile:75-79), so the final artifact is clean. The exposure is the build context transfer and the builder layer cache on whatever machine runs the documented `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d --build` (docker-compose.dev.yml:14).
impact: Local image builds copy hundreds of megabytes of irrelevant tree, including a second full checkout, into the daemon and the layer cache, slowing every build. A nested .env with real values sits in the builder layer, which is retained in the local build cache and would be pushed if anyone ever added a cache-export or a stage that copies more broadly. Real but bounded, because the shipped image is unaffected today.
recommendation: Change the patterns in .dockerignore to their recursive forms (`**/.env`, `**/.env.*`, `**/node_modules`) and add `.claude`, `audits`, `databases`, `marketing`, `coverage`, `graphify-out` and `docker-compose.dev.yml`. Keep the `!.env.example` re-include after the broadened dotenv rules.

title: Five pairs of /checks pages ship an identical H1 and an identical title tag, including two Django debug pages with identical fix steps, so each pair competes with itself for the same query
description: Scanning the raw `title` field of all 749 non-disabled checks in lib/scanner/checks-data/*.json for case-insensitive duplicates gives five pairs, all of which produce two URLs with the same <title>, the same og:title, and the same H1 (app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:196 renders `How to fix: {check.title}`): "Sensitive information in HTML comments" (/checks/sensitive-comments and /checks/html-comment-leaks), "Weak or broken cryptography detected" (/checks/weak-crypto and /checks/insecure-crypto), "document.write() Usage Detected" (/checks/document-write-usage in content.json at low severity and /checks/cs-document-write-usage in client-side.json at high), "eval() Usage Detected" (/checks/eval-usage in code.json and /checks/vibe-eval-usage in vibe-code.json), and "Django debug mode enabled in production" (/checks/django-debug-page in content.json and /checks/django-debug-page-exposure in information-disclosure.json). The Django pair is the closest: both are critical, both have a byte-identical fixSteps array ["Set DEBUG = False in production settings", "Set ALLOWED_HOSTS to your actual domain names", "Configure a proper error logging backend (Sentry, logging module)"], and their riskImpact sentences differ only in wording. Meta descriptions do differ across all five pairs, so this is duplicate titles and headings rather than duplicate documents. These pairs also account for 6 of the 22 pages in the seo-03 title-collision set.
impact: Ten URLs, five queries, and for each query Google picks one page and treats the other as a near-duplicate to filter out of results. "django debug mode enabled in production" is a real search with real volume and the site answers it twice with the same words, which splits any signal either page would otherwise accumulate.
recommendation: Two options per pair. Where both checks are genuinely distinct detectors (the document.write pair genuinely differs: one is a low-severity content scan, the other a high-severity client-side script scan), differentiate the title in the JSON data itself: "document.write() in page scripts (client-side scan)" versus "document.write() in response body (content scan)". Where they are the same finding twice (the Django pair, whose fix steps are byte-identical), pick the canonical URL and have the other's generateMetadata set `alternates: { canonical: `/checks/${primaryId}` }`, which keeps both URLs live for deep links from a scan result while consolidating the ranking signal. pageMetadata (lib/seo/metadata.ts:83) already takes the canonical from `path`, so this needs a new optional `canonicalPath` option on PageSeoOptions.

title: The OG image build script imports sharp, which is not declared in any package.json and is only present as an optional transitive dependency of next
description: scripts/build-og-image.mjs:11 does `import sharp from "sharp"` and is the only way to regenerate public/og-image.png from public/og-image.svg. sharp appears in neither `dependencies` nor `devDependencies` of the root package.json; it resolves today only because it is an optional dependency of next (package-lock.json:9804 lists `"sharp": "^0.34.3"` under next), and the root `overrides` block pins it to ^0.35.0 without declaring it. Any install with `--omit=optional`, any next major that stops shipping sharp, or a platform where sharp's optional binary does not install, makes the script fail with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. The script's own header comment says it is deliberately not a build hook, so the failure only surfaces when someone next edits the card, which is the moment they least want to debug a toolchain.
impact: The OG image is, per AUDIT-011, one of the three strongest design artifacts the project owns, and the only script that can rebuild it depends on a package nothing declares. A self-hoster or contributor who rebrands by editing og-image.svg hits an install error rather than a rebuilt card. Low blast radius but it is squarely on the path of the seo-02 work, which will want the same sharp pipeline.
recommendation: Add `"sharp": "^0.35.0"` to devDependencies in the root package.json so the existing `overrides` entry has something to override and the script has a declared dependency. Do NOT regenerate package-lock.json on Windows to do it: per this repo's history, a Windows-regenerated lockfile strips the Linux native bindings and breaks CI and deploy. Add the entry and graft the corresponding lock nodes, or make the change on Linux/CI. If seo-02 uses next/og instead (which is bundled with next and needs no new dependency), the script can stay as the one sharp consumer.

title: There is no offline signal anywhere in the app or the extension's web surfaces, so one dropped connection produces a different and mostly wrong message on every screen
description: Grepping `navigator.onLine`, the `online`/`offline` window events and any equivalent across app/, components/, lib/ and extension/src returns only an unrelated staff-status filter string (components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx:71). Nothing in the product knows it is offline. Each surface therefore renders whatever its own catch does for a network failure, and those disagree: /history renders the "No scans recorded yet" empty state (AUDIT-011#hist-02, still present at app/history/page.tsx:231-232), the dashboard analytics renders nothing (AUDIT-011#dash-01, components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:229), /admin renders "Access Denied" (state-10), the notification bell renders "All caught up!" (state-11), the profile Developer tab renders "you have no API keys" (state-05), and the scan form is the only one that gets it right, because components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:96-104 has a dedicated `network` kind with accurate copy. The extension is the one surface with a real connectivity concept, `connectionFailed` from refreshMe (extension/src/popup/popup.ts:1050) rendered as "Failed to connect" by extension/src/popup/components/connect-pill.ts:38-42, though it points the user at Settings, which is the wrong remedy for a network outage.
impact: Losing wifi in a tunnel or on a flaky connection tells the user, depending on which tab they are on, that their scan history was deleted, that they are not an administrator, and that they have no API keys. Each of those is individually filed above; the shared root is that no component can tell a network failure from a server rejection, so each one guesses, and the guesses are wrong in the alarming direction.
recommendation: Add a small `useOnline()` hook in lib/hooks/ backed by navigator.onLine plus the online/offline window events, and a single app-level band rendered from app/layout.tsx that says "You're offline. Nothing here is up to date." Then let list components read it to choose their message: while offline, a failed fetch renders "Can't reach the server" rather than an empty state, everywhere, without each component needing its own classifier. components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx already models the classified-error approach and its `network` entry is the copy to reuse. In the extension, change connect-pill.ts:38-42 so `connectionFailed` offers "Retry" rather than "Settings", since a network failure is not a key problem.

title: CLI has one 81-line test for 254 lines of source, and marketing/ has none, leaving the two smaller packages effectively unverified
description: cli/ is a standalone dependency-free Node package excluded from the app's tsc, eslint, and vitest, with its own `node --test` suite that CI does run (.github/workflows/ci.yml, 'Run CLI unit tests'). The suite is one file, cli/vulnradar.test.mjs at 81 lines, against cli/lib.mjs (136 lines) plus cli/vulnradar.mjs (118 lines). No coverage is collected for it, so the tested fraction is unknown, but 81 lines of test against 254 lines of source that includes argument parsing, API-key handling, and output formatting is thin. marketing/ is a separate Remotion project with its own package.json and node_modules and no test setup or CI job at all; that is defensible for a video project and is noted for completeness rather than as an action item.
impact: The CLI is a published entry point that carries a user's API key. A regression in argument parsing or in how the key is read and sent is caught only if it happens to break the single existing suite. The blast radius is smaller than the extension's (cov-14) because a CLI fix ships immediately with no store review.
recommendation: Add `--experimental-test-coverage` to the CLI's test script so the number is at least visible, then extend cli/vulnradar.test.mjs to cover each subcommand's argument parsing, the missing-API-key path, a non-200 API response, and the JSON versus human output formats. Leave marketing/ as is.

title: Two more empty leftover directories beyond the one already filed, both from the removed admin bulk feature and a removed admin users test suite
description: AUDIT-011#bulk-06 filed the empty app/api/v3/admin/bulk/. Sweeping the whole working tree for empty directories (excluding node_modules, .git, .next, coverage, graphify-out, marketing and .claude) turns up four, of which two are new: tests/app/api/v3/admin/bulk/, the test directory that mirrored the same removed admin bulk endpoint, and tests/components/admin/users/, which has no counterpart suite anywhere (components/admin/users/ still exists with user-detail-panel.tsx, and its only test lives at tests/components/admin/utils.test.ts). The fourth, scripts/storage/json/, is a runtime output directory that .gitignore covers at 'scripts/storage/' and should be left alone. Note that git does not track empty directories, so none of these appear in git ls-files and a fresh clone will not have them: they are working-tree residue from deleted files, which is also why they survived AUDIT-011's fix of the sibling directory.
impact: Small but real: an empty tests/app/api/v3/admin/bulk/ next to a live tests/app/api/v3/admin/ makes it look as though bulk admin actions have route tests when they have none, and vitest's include glob 'tests/**/*.test.ts' silently collects nothing from them. Directory listings and editor file trees carry a feature that no longer exists.
recommendation: Remove the directories tests/app/api/v3/admin/bulk/ and tests/components/admin/users/ from the working tree at the same time as app/api/v3/admin/bulk/ from AUDIT-011#bulk-06. Leave scripts/storage/json/ alone. Because git does not track empty directories this is a local cleanup with no commit, so it must be done on each checkout that has the residue.

title: Nothing in scripts/ or cli/ gets any static analysis: eslint ignores both directories and tsconfig covers neither, which is why a broken import in an 872-line script went unnoticed
description: eslint.config.mjs:22-36 sets ignores including 'scripts/**' and 'cli/**'. tsconfig.json includes only '**/*.ts', '**/*.tsx' and '**/*.d.ts' and excludes 'scripts/create-fresh-db/schemas/**' and 'cli/**', so the 51 .mjs files under scripts/ (13,161 lines per the brief's measurement of scripts/) are matched by neither: not by 'npm run lint' (CI, .github/workflows/ci.yml:39) and not by 'npx tsc --noEmit' (CI, ci.yml:63). The CLI does get its node:test suite run in CI (ci.yml:109-111) but no lint or typecheck. The practical consequence is dead-04: scripts/migrate/versions/_legacy-original.mjs:47 imports 22 symbols from './_lib.mjs', a path that does not resolve, and no gate in the repository notices. ESLint's default recommended set (reached here through eslint-config-next/core-web-vitals) carries no-unreachable, no-dupe-else-if, no-constant-condition and no-undef as errors, which is why app/, lib/ and components/ are clean of those classes: I found zero unreachable branches and zero duplicate else-if conditions there, and exactly two identical-arm ternaries (dead-07). scripts/ and cli/ have had no such sweep at any point. A second, smaller symptom in the same tree: scripts/migrate/_meta.mjs:82 exports META_TABLE_NAME (a re-export of the module-local META_TABLE) which nothing imports anywhere in the repo, the kind of thing an unused-export rule reports for free.
impact: Migration and database-repair scripts are the code with the highest blast radius in this repository and the least checking. A typo'd import, an unreachable branch, or a reference to a renamed helper in scripts/migrate/ or scripts/db-repair*.mjs fails at runtime on an operator's populated database rather than in CI, which is the same failure mode that dead-04 is already sitting on.
recommendation: Remove 'scripts/**' and 'cli/**' from the ignores array in eslint.config.mjs:22-36 and add a minimal flat-config block for them (languageOptions.globals node, sourceType module) so at least the recommended correctness rules run. Add 'npm run lint' coverage of .mjs by including it in the eslint invocation. Expect a first-run backlog of warnings: land the config with only the error-level correctness rules enabled if the style backlog is too large to fix in one pass.

title: db:restore feeds GCM plaintext into psql before the auth tag is verified, so a corrupted or tampered backup is partially applied before the integrity check fails
description: For an .enc backup, runRestore builds `pipeline(source, decipher, decrypted)` at line 84 and immediately assigns the PassThrough to `source` (line 88), then at line 106 pipes it through gunzip into psql's stdin. AES-256-GCM emits plaintext as it decrypts and only validates the auth tag set at line 82 when the final block is processed, so by the time an authentication failure surfaces, every preceding block has already been gunzipped and executed by psql. The failure handler (line 85) prints "Decryption failed" and calls process.exit(1), leaving the already-executed statements committed, since psql is running without --single-transaction (see migrate-04).
impact: The whole point of authenticating the backup is to guarantee that a modified or truncated dump is never applied. As written, an attacker who can modify a backup file, or plain bit rot in cold storage, results in a partially applied dump plus an error message, rather than a clean refusal. Low severity because it requires an already-compromised or corrupted backup artifact, and because the operator does see a failure message.
recommendation: Decrypt and verify to a temporary file first, and only start psql once the decipher stream has ended without error, deleting the temp file in a finally. Alternatively keep the streaming path but combine it with `--single-transaction` on psql (already recommended in migrate-04) so a late decryption failure rolls back everything that was streamed.

title: Fourteen tests assert only .not.toThrow(), and two of them name a behavioural contract the assertion never checks
description:
A scripted pass over all 4,494 it/test blocks found 14 whose every expect matcher is `not.toThrow`. Most are honest ("does not throw on truncated markup"), but two claim a behaviour they do not verify. tests/lib/scanner/safety-rating.test.ts:215 is titled "falls back to a default weight for an unrecognized severity string" and its whole body is `expect(() => getDangerScore([{ severity: "unknown", title: "Something Odd" }])).not.toThrow()`. The fallback it names is lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts:327, `const baseWeight = SEVERITY_WEIGHTS[sev] ?? 0.1`. Exact mutation not caught: change `?? 0.1` to `?? 10` and the test passes, while every scan containing one finding with an unrecognised severity string jumps to the top of the danger scale and the site is reported unsafe. tests/lib/scanner/html/tokenizer.test.ts:103 is titled "does not create an element for an end tag with no matching start" and asserts only `expect(() => toElements(tokenize("

ok

"))).not.toThrow()`. Exact mutation not caught: make toElements emit an element for the stray ``, and the test passes while every page check that counts or walks elements sees a phantom node. The other 12 are: tests/lib/api/playground.test.ts:67, tests/lib/api/request-utils.test.ts:93, tests/lib/auth/password-hash.test.ts:45, tests/lib/backup/job-store.test.ts:53 and :57, tests/lib/database/error-log-capture.test.ts:87, tests/lib/scanner/engine.test.ts:72 (filed separately as tq-03), tests/lib/scanner/html/tokenizer.test.ts:68, tests/lib/scanner/page-context.test.ts:144, tests/lib/scanner/scan-jobs.test.ts:155, tests/lib/ui/url-state.test.ts:66, tests/lib/updater/job-store.test.ts:52.
impact: Two named contracts, the danger-score fallback weight and the tokenizer's stray-end-tag handling, have a test that reads as covering them in a coverage review but cannot fail on a wrong answer, only on a crash. The danger score is the number shown to users as the site's safety rating, so a wrong fallback weight is directly user visible.
recommendation:
In tests/lib/scanner/safety-rating.test.ts:215, assert the score itself: compare `getDangerScore([{ severity: "unknown", ... }])` against the value implied by the 0.1 weight, and add a sibling case proving an unknown severity scores strictly below an info finding. In tests/lib/scanner/html/tokenizer.test.ts:103, assert `toElements(tokenize("

ok

")).map(e => e.tag)` equals `["p"]`. Leave the other 12 as they are; their titles match what they assert.

title: Thirteen tests assert only that a value exists (toBeDefined / toBeTruthy / not.toBeNull) where the contract they name is the value's content
description: Scripted over all 4,494 blocks: 13 have no assertion stronger than a positive-existence matcher. The ones where the content is the actual contract: tests/lib/scanner/checks-data/_schema.test.ts:77 "every entry has required fields" loops the required list (id, title, category, severity, description, evidence, fixSteps, codeExamples) and asserts `expect(entry[field]).toBeDefined()` at lines 90 to 93, so an entry shipped with `description: ""`, `fixSteps: []`, or `codeExamples: []` passes the only required-fields guard the whole 750-plus check catalogue has. tests/lib/scanner/auth/logout-guard.test.ts:63 "returns a non-secret reason for a destructive URL" asserts only `expect(reason).toBeTruthy()`, so a reason that does leak a credential or query string passes, even though the sibling test at :55 to :60 does run a `not.toMatch(/password|cookie=|token=/i)` check for a different URL. tests/lib/scanner/registry.test.ts:119 is titled "etag-inode uses the real headers.ts detector, not configuration.ts's disabled stub" but asserts the fired finding is defined rather than asserting its identity, the way the sibling tests at :107 and :128 do. Three worker suites (tests/lib/backup/scheduled-backup-worker.test.ts:102, tests/lib/domains/reverify-worker.test.ts:167, tests/lib/notifications/posture-digest.test.ts:331) each assert `toBeDefined` on "registers a timer and cleanly cancels it" without asserting the interval passed to setInterval or that cancel actually clears the same handle. The remaining cases are weaker in form than in substance: tests/lib/auth/password-strength.test.ts:355 and :363 end in `toBeDefined` but pin the text inside the preceding `.find(w => w.includes(...))`, and the four in tests/lib/auth/authorization.test.ts (:128, :146, :159, :228) use `not.toBeNull` as an allow/deny signal that the `it.each` at :95 already backs with an exact object comparison.
impact: Each of these reads as covering a named behaviour but only fails if the code returns nothing at all. The _schema.test.ts:77 case is the widest: it is the single guard over the whole JSON check catalogue and it accepts empty strings and empty arrays for every required field, so a check shipped with a blank description or no fix steps reaches the ~750 public /checks SEO pages and the scan result UI with nothing to render.
recommendation: Tighten the content assertions: in _schema.test.ts:77 replace `toBeDefined` with a non-empty check per field (a string field must be a non-empty string, fixSteps and codeExamples must be non-empty arrays); in logout-guard.test.ts:63 apply the same `not.toMatch(/password|cookie=|token=/i)` assertion the sibling test at :60 already uses; in registry.test.ts:119 assert the detector's identity the way :107 and :128 do; in the three worker suites assert the interval argument passed to setInterval and that clearInterval was called with the same handle.

title: no-floating-promises is scoped to four auth path globs, so 86 no-op .catch handlers and 8 empty catch blocks in the scanner, billing and webhook paths pass lint
description: eslint.config.mjs's type-aware block enables `@typescript-eslint/no-floating-promises` (:126) and `no-misused-promises` (:122) only for the four globs listed at :108-113 (`lib/auth/**/*.ts`, `app/api/v3/auth/**/*.ts`, `app/api/v3/account/**/*.ts`, `app/api/v3/admin/**/*.ts`), and the main rules block (:58-92) enables no rule against empty catch blocks. A scan of the 965 source files under app/, lib/, components/, extension/src/, cli/ and scripts/ finds 8 statement-level `catch {}` blocks with a genuinely empty body, 183 with only a comment, and 86 inline `.catch(() => {})` / `.catch(() => null)` no-op handlers. Most of the 183 are deliberate and documented (a scanner check whose DNS lookup failing genuinely means no finding), which is exactly why the raw count is not itself the finding: the finding is that nothing distinguishes the deliberate ones from the ones filed above as obs-01 and obs-06, and nothing stops the next one being added.
impact: The swallowed-error findings in this section (obs-01 in the scan engine, obs-06 in metering and quota refunds) all live in directories the lint rules do not cover, and none of them would be flagged today. The pattern reproduces on every new file in lib/scanner, lib/billing, lib/webhooks and lib/email.
recommendation: Extend the type-aware `files` list in eslint.config.mjs:108-113 to include `lib/billing/**/*.ts`, `lib/webhooks/**/*.ts`, `lib/email/**/*.ts` and `lib/scanner/*.ts` (the orchestration files, not the 4000-line check bodies, to keep lint time bounded). Add `"no-empty": ["error", { allowEmptyCatch: false }]` to the main rules block so a new bare `catch {}` has to be written as a commented no-op or a logged one.

title: The safe-fetch test suite covers redirects and IPv6 canonicalization but never exercises the address-range gaps, the allowedHostnames argument, or any body bound
category: test gap in the SSRF guard
description:
tests/lib/scanner/safe-fetch.test.ts is 231 lines and 18 cases. It mocks dns/promises (:6-9) and stubs global fetch (:127-131), and it does cover the things prior audits broke: IPv6 canonicalization of ::1 / ::ffff:127.0.0.1 / 64:ff9b:: forms (:21-79), resolve-to-private (:83), the metadata IP (:91), fail-closed on empty DNS (:104) and on DNS error (:204), the redirect-to-metadata and redirect-to-RFC1918 refusals (:141, :156), cross-host redirect refusal (:169), same-host rebind refusal (:184), and the non-http scheme refusal (:227). So the memory note that safeFetch had ZERO tests is stale.

What is not covered maps one-to-one onto the defects filed above:
- No case asserts any bound on the response body, in bytes or in time: the behaviour in ssrf-01 would pass the suite unchanged.
- No case for the `allowedHostnames` parameter (lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:574-582), even though it is the stated containment for every active probe (lib/scanner/active-probes/shared.ts:14-19) and it is enforced only on the first hop, not on the www-apex redirect the loop permits.
- No case for the `session` parameter's credential-drop-on-redirect behaviour (lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:671-680), the whole reason authenticated scanning is safe.
- No case for 100.64/10, 198.18/15 or 192.0.0.0/24 (ssrf-03), nor for the fe80::/10 and fc00::/7 prefix widths (ssrf-05).
- No case for pinToResolvedIp (lib/scanner/safe-fetch.ts:273) or for the fact that the HTTPS branch does not pin (ssrf-02).
