- No case for a hostname in decimal/octal/hex form, which currently relies entirely on getaddrinfo normalising before isPrivateIP runs.
impact: The guard is the single most consequential piece of code in the product, and the parts of it that are currently wrong are exactly the parts with no test. Any of the fixes recommended in ssrf-01 through ssrf-05 can be shipped, then silently regressed, with a green suite.
recommendation: Extend tests/lib/scanner/safe-fetch.test.ts with: a case that stubs fetch with a Response over a never-ending ReadableStream and asserts safeFetch's consumer stops at the byte cap and within the deadline; a case asserting safeFetch rejects a hostname absent from allowedHostnames, and one asserting the www-apex redirect hop is re-checked against that list; a case asserting session headers are attached on-origin and absent after a redirect; table cases for 100.100.100.200, 198.18.0.1, 192.0.0.1, fe81::1, fcff::1 in the existing isPrivateIP block at :21; and a case asserting the fetch dispatcher connects to the validated IP for an https target once ssrf-02 is fixed.

title: GitHub AI repo-review endpoint makes real GitHub API calls before its quota/rate gate
description: POST /api/v3/scan/github calls getRepoInfo and listRepoTree (real GitHub API requests using the user's connected token) before checkGithubReviewQuota runs. Every other AI-adjacent or expensive endpoint in this app (chat, verify, verify-batch, bulk scan, crawl, discover, demo-scan, browser sessions) goes through checkRateLimit first; this one has no per-request throttle at all, only a per-day quota check that happens after the two GitHub API round-trips. Impact is mostly limited to the calling user's own GitHub API rate limit rather than a shared resource, so this is low severity, but it's the one gap in an otherwise consistently-applied pattern. Evidence: app/api/v3/scan/github/route.ts lines 73-119 (getRepoInfo/listRepoTree calls precede the checkGithubReviewQuota call at line 116); no import of checkRateLimit anywhere in that file (confirmed via grep, contrasted with every sibling route under app/api/v3/scan/).
recommendation: NOT YET APPLIED -- reported for review. Recommendation: Add a checkRateLimit gate (a new named limit, e.g. githubReview) at the top of the handler, before any GitHub API call, mirroring the pattern already used everywhere else.

title: Badge stats endpoint compares the share token in plaintext against scan_history.share_token instead of the hashed lookup used identically elsewhere, and silently ignores host_badges auto-updating tokens
description: app/api/v3/badge/[token]/stats/route.ts queries `WHERE sh.share_token = $1` (the raw plaintext token from the URL) rather than hashing it and comparing against share_token_hash, unlike the sibling badge image route (app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts) and the shared-report route (app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts), both of which deliberately hash first with a comment citing AUDIT-004#secrets-01 ('so the plaintext token is never compared directly in the DB'). Since share_token_hash is a Postgres GENERATED column computed from share_token in the same row, this isn't a new confidentiality gap (the plaintext already lives in that row either way) and 256 bits of entropy makes any timing-based guessing attack infeasible regardless -- so this is a consistency/defense-in-depth gap, not a demonstrated exploit path. Separately, this endpoint never queries host_badges at all, so it silently 404s for any of the new auto-updating badge tokens created via POST /api/v3/badge/site -- a functional gap parallel to the two routes it's supposed to mirror. Evidence: app/api/v3/badge/[token]/stats/route.ts:19-25 (`WHERE sh.share_token = $1`, no hashing, no host_badges fallback) vs. app/api/v3/badge/[token]/route.ts:39-73 and app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:24-60 (both hash-then-compare and both fall back to host_badges).
recommendation: NOT YET APPLIED -- reported for review. Recommendation: Hash the incoming token with SHA-256 and compare against share_token_hash for consistency with the two sibling routes, and add the same host_badges fallback query so stats work for auto-updating badges too.

title: db:migrate and db:create cannot be driven non-interactively -- piped stdin hangs forever
description: Each prompt in _lib.prompts.mjs and _lib.target.mjs opens a brand-new readline.Interface and closes it after a single answer. When multiple newline-separated answers are piped into stdin at once, Node's readline greedily buffers the whole pipe into the first Interface; only the first line is consumed before that Interface is discarded, and every later prompt then blocks forever with no timeout or error. Reproduced twice. Both scripts must be run attached to a real TTY with a human typing each answer; they cannot be scripted, used in CI, or wired into an automated deploy step.
recommendation: Create one shared readline.Interface per script run in _lib.prompts.mjs and _lib.target.mjs and reuse it across every ask/askYesNo/chooseDatabase call instead of opening and closing a new one per question.

title: Verified correct: the compiled AI knowledge is byte-identical to a fresh compile, and the CLI, plan quotas, active-probe ids, crawl quota semantics, reports and triage pages all match the code
description: Recorded so the next audit does not redo the work. (1) lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md is in sync: re-running a redirected copy of scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs against the current app/docs tree produced a file differing only in the `_Auto-compiled ... on <date>_` line, so no docs page has been edited without a recompile. impact: None. Documents what was checked and found correct so a later audit can skip it.

title: Negative results: pipeline secrets handling is clean, every action is SHA-pinned, and the release artifact chain works end to end
description: Verified so the next audit does not repeat it. (1) No workflow uses `pull_request_target`, `secrets: inherit`, or `workflow_call`; grep across .github/ returns nothing for all three. (2) The only secret referenced anywhere in .github/ is `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` (7 references across 5 files); no third-party credential is present in the pipeline. (3) No secret is passed as a Docker build arg or baked into an image ENV: Dockerfile:16 declares only `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` as an ARG and lines 37-40 set placeholder values, with the comment at 41-44 explaining that API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY is deliberately left unset so it fails closed. (4) No untrusted `github.event.*` field is interpolated into a `run:` body; release.yml routes `release.tag_name` and `workflow_run.head_branch` through `env:` at lines 86-88 with a comment naming the CodeQL rule, and docker-publish.yml:40 and 43 use the `GITHUB_REF_NAME` and `GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER` shell variables rather than expressions. (5) All 23 `uses:` lines across the seven workflows are pinned to a 40-character commit SHA with a version comment (23 of 23 match `@[0-9a-f]{40}`). (6) Permissions are scoped per workflow or per job everywhere except label.yml (see ci-05); ci.yml is `contents: read`, docker-publish.yml scopes `packages: write` and `id-token: write` to the one job that needs them, release.yml scopes `contents: write` and `id-token: write` to its one job. (7) `continue-on-error` appears exactly once (release.yml:168, see ci-12) and there is no `|| true` anywhere. (8) `npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev` currently reports 0 vulnerabilities, so the gate at ci.yml:71 is passing rather than being routed around. (9) next.config.mjs sets no `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors`; `eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds: true` at line 23 is compensated by the standalone `npm run lint` step at ci.yml:40. `output: "standalone"` is deliberately absent and consistent with Dockerfile:75-79 copying `.next` and `node_modules` (line 4-8 comment). (10) The CI knowledge-drift gate works: I confirmed empirically that `git diff --exit-code --ignore-matching-lines='compiled from'` ignores a date-only change and still exits 1 on a real content change, and the date lines in all five generated files contain the string "compiled from". (11) The release artifact chain is live and correct: I fetched the releases API and v3.6.0 through v3.7.2 each carry the tarball, the `.tar.gz.cert` cosign bundle, `sha256sums.txt`, both extension zips, and the CycloneDX SBOM, and the asset names match exactly what lib/updater/apply.ts:85-88 looks for. (12) Nothing can publish an image from a branch push: docker-publish.yml triggers only on `push: tags: v*`.
impact: None. This records what was checked and found correct.
recommendation: No action. Re-verify items 5, 6 and 8 if new workflows are added.

title: Container, IaC, cloud and SCA scanning and an IAST agent are real competitor features that this product should deliberately never build, and saying so is part of the answer
category: list (a) ranks 16 to 18: the deliberate do-not-build list
description: Three capabilities appear in the peer set and belong at the bottom of the ranking with a stated reason rather than in a backlog. (1) Container, IaC, cloud and SCA scanning: Snyk is the only vendor of the eight spanning SAST, SCA, container, IaC, secrets, DAST and SBOM, and the best tool in that space is Trivy, which is free, Apache-2.0, 37,679 stars, emits SARIF 2.1.0 and CycloneDX/SPDX, and would take years to match. VulnRadar's nearest existing capability is deliberately narrow and correct: lib/scanner/github-repo-scan.ts:1 reuses the secrets-extended detectors verbatim against repo file contents, and lib/scanner/software-inventory.ts plus osv-check.ts correlate detected libraries against OSV for the live URL. (2) An IAST agent: only Acunetix ships one (AcuSensor, for PHP, ASP.NET, Java and Node.js), and none of the other seven has a comparable server-side sensor. It would require a per-runtime agent, an installation story, and version support forever, and it directly contradicts the product's own repeated promise that there is nothing to deploy alongside your application (components/landing/landing-features.tsx:4, app/checks/page.tsx's "0 agents to install"). (3) An internal or behind-the-firewall scanning agent, which Snyk and Intruder both ship as a Docker or Kubernetes workload: for this product the self-host path is the answer to that requirement and is strictly better, since the whole scanner runs inside the network rather than a relay.
impact: None if left alone. The risk this finding addresses is the opposite one: each of these is impressive on a competitor's feature matrix, and a small team that chases them spends quarters reaching parity in a market it is not in, while the cheap items in comp-02, comp-03, comp-04, comp-06 and comp-07 stay unbuilt.
recommendation: Record all three as permanent non-goals in AGENTS.md or a short ROADMAP note so they stop reappearing. For (1), do the interop instead of the feature: document the pairing in app/docs ("Trivy for images and dependencies, VulnRadar for the deployed URL"), and since both emit SARIF 2.1.0, both already land in the same GitHub Security tab with no work. For (3), make the self-host answer explicit on the relevant /alternatives rows rather than building an agent: "They give you a relay container. This runs the whole scanner inside your network." That claim depends on comp-01 being fixed first.

title: Negative results: every documented npm command exists, all 25 docs anchors resolve, the CLI help matches its implementation, and every SECURITY-POSTURE part A control is really in middleware

(7) CONTRIBUTING.md's 'all commits to main must be GPG-signed' holds: the last twelve commits all report %G? = G. (8) CLAUDE.md's file-map table resolves for all 15 paths, and its browser-session note (1 minute start, +1 minute, 5 minute max) matches app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:126, :196 and :287. impact: None. Recorded to save the next audit the work and to bound where the real problems are: the failures in this section are concentrated in stale architecture prose and in operator recovery procedures, not in command names or links.
recommendation: No action. If a link or command checker is ever wanted in CI, the three throwaway scripts used here (command extraction against package.json, internal href resolution against app/ page.tsx and route.ts, anchor resolution against id= attributes) are each about 60 lines and run in under a second on this repo.

title: Verified clean: the docs surface, the email layout, and the Markdown and SARIF severity vocabulary are all consistent systems, and the AUDIT-013 label inconsistency does not reach any export
description: Recording what was checked and found correct, so the next audit does not repeat it. (1) DOCS ARE ONE SYSTEM. All 19 docs pages plus app/docs/page.tsx use DocsHero and DocsSection; the chrome (breadcrumb, prev/next pager, table of contents, sidebar, mobile nav) lives once in components/docs/docs-shell.tsx:60-90 and is applied by app/docs/layout.tsx to every page, so no page can forget it. Hand-rolled cards outside the primitives total 7 across 12,000 lines of docs pages (2 in api, 3 in setup, 1 each in developers and rate-limits) and there are zero hand-rolled `<table>` elements. DocsCallout (components/docs/docs-callout.tsx:12-18) draws its four variants from semantic tokens with a left rule and an explicit docblock rejecting the icon-in-a-rounded-square. The open docs issues remain AUDIT-011#docs-03 (124-character measure), #docs-04 (shell wider than its nav), #docs-07 (unlabelled playground inputs) and #docs-11 (tablist without tabpanel); nothing new was found. (2) EMAIL HAS THE SHARED LAYOUT IT NEEDS. lib/email/email.ts:107-180 is a single layout() used by every template through sendEmail:431, with seven composition helpers (:193-332), an escapeHtml applied at every interpolation, a plain-text alternative on every template (47 `text:` keys against 46 `html:`), zero emoji, zero em dashes in user-facing strings, a 600px table with a max-width:600px media query and mobile padding overrides (:138-141), `color-scheme` and `supported-color-schemes` meta (:133-134) which is the correct guard against forced dark-mode inversion, and colours sourced from lib/config/brand.ts rather than hardcoded (:19-46). Copy voice follows the rules: mechanism-first, specific, no platitudes. The open items are dsnx-05, dsnx-06 and dsnx-11 only. (3) SEVERITY VOCABULARY IN EXPORTS IS CONSISTENT. AUDIT-013#dup-02 found `/checks` labelling info as "Informational" (lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:30) against "Info" elsewhere. That inconsistency does NOT reach any export: markdown-report.ts:31-37 and compliance-report.ts:29-34 both use "Info", pdf-report.ts:273 prints `sev.toUpperCase()`, sarif-report.ts maps to SARIF's own three levels, and CSV uses `f.severity.toUpperCase()`. Ordering is critical-to-info in all five, and findings arrive pre-sorted from lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:711. "Informational" appears in only three places repo-wide and none of them is an export. (4) THE EXTENSION POPUP DOES MATCH ITS STORE ART. store_1.png's product panel shows a risk score with a label, a severity chip row, findings with coloured left rails, and a footer with a finding count and a "Full report" link; extension/src/popup/popup.ts:331-430 renders exactly that structure, including the 3px severity rail at :508. The store screenshots are honest about the shipped UI. (5) NO HTML REPORT RENDERER EXISTS. The export set is JSON, CSV, PDF, SARIF, Markdown and the compliance crosswalk; the shared scan page at /shared/[token] is the de facto HTML report and belongs to the in-app review.
impact: None. This is a record of coverage. It matters mainly for the two surfaces auditors most expect to be broken and which are not: the email system already has the shared layout that usually needs to be proposed, and the docs already read as one manual rather than twenty pages.
recommendation: No action. When re-auditing section 5, start from the report renderers and the extension, which is where the real drift is, and treat lib/email/email.ts and components/docs/ as reference implementations of what a shared abstraction should look like on the other surfaces.

(2) Scanner identity: every outbound User-Agent is built from APP_NAME (nine sites, listed in hc-14). (3) SEO plumbing: app/sitemap.ts:16, app/robots.ts:88-89 and app/layout.tsx:122 (metadataBase) all derive from APP_URL, and app/robots.ts:79 uses APP_NAME as the self-referential crawler token. (4) app/api/security-txt/route.ts:19 correctly resolves SECURITY_EMAIL through getSetting, and LEGAL_EMAIL/SECURITY_EMAIL/ENTERPRISE_EMAIL reach the /legal/* pages the same way. (5) Badge and share embed snippets at app/docs/sharing/page.tsx:386 and :391 are built from APP_URL. (6) The GitHub Action (.github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml:15-18) and the GitLab template (public/gitlab/vulnradar-scan.gitlab-ci.yml:31) both expose the API base as a documented input for self-hosted use. (7) The self-updater derives its release source from APP_REPO (lib/updater/github-release.ts:28, lib/updater/cosign.ts:22). (8) No hardcoded third-party credentials or object IDs anywhere: no Stripe price_/prod_ literals, Browserbase project id and API key are env-only (lib/browserbase/client.ts:94-139), Turnstile and Google Web Risk likewise, and there is no analytics ID in the app at all. (9) Filesystem paths: no absolute or Windows-shaped path in any runtime module; the four writable locations all derive from process.cwd() or an env override (app/api/v3/admin/backup/route.ts:27 BACKUP_DIR, lib/uploads/avatar-migration.ts:49, lib/backup/run-backup.ts:30, lib/updater/apply.ts:130 which correctly uses os.tmpdir()). (10) The two DoH resolvers at lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:843-849 and :1758-1762 (dns.google, cloudflare-dns.com) are hardcoded but redundant with each other and are a scanner dependency rather than a deployment-identity value, so they are noted here rather than filed.
impact: None. This is the verified-correct half of the deployment-identity sweep, recorded to bound the problem: the hardcoding in this codebase is concentrated in the config-resolution layer (hc-01, hc-03, hc-06, hc-07), the extension (hc-02) and the Docker image contents (hc-04), not spread through the application code.
recommendation: No action. If a future audit re-runs this section, start from lib/config/registry.ts's tier field and the getSetting call graph rather than from a grep for the domain: the grep is clean and the defects are all in whether a resolved value is actually read.

title: Negative results for the next audit: root .env.local is correctly excluded from the image, the container runs non-root with a real healthcheck and shutdown handlers, and Stripe, AI, Turnstile and Browserbase all degrade gracefully when unset
description: Recorded so the next audit does not re-derive them. All static, nothing executed. (1) Secret leak into the image: root .env.local IS matched by both `.env.*` and `.env*.local` at .dockerignore:5-6 and never enters the context; `!.env.example` at :7 correctly re-includes only the template. The nested caveat is host-11. (2) The `*.md` exclusion at .dockerignore:9 is root-anchored and therefore does not strip the five generated AI knowledge files under lib/ai/, and the prebuild compilers (package.json:13) read .ts sources (scripts/compile-changelog-knowledge.mjs:26 reads lib/changelog/data.ts), so the build is not broken by it. (3) Non-root: Dockerfile:71-72 creates uid/gid 1001 and :102 switches to it before EXPOSE. (4) HEALTHCHECK at Dockerfile:99-100 and docker-compose.yml:87-99 both target /api/v3/health, which does a real pool.connect plus a schema-version and required-tables probe (app/api/v3/health/route.ts:88-116) rather than the GitHub-only /api/version, and the path is in lib/config/public-paths.ts:109 so middleware does not block the probe. (5) Compose ordering is correct: the app depends_on postgres with condition: service_healthy (docker-compose.yml:79-81) against a pg_isready healthcheck (:26-30), so there is no startup race. postgres_data (:115) persists across `docker compose down`, and app/docs/setup/page.tsx:679-680 correctly flags `down -v` as the destructive variant. (6) Postgres 16.4-alpine (:18) satisfies the documented 14+ floor in README.md:124. (7) Graceful shutdown: SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers close the pool at the end of instrumentation.ts's register(), and tini is PID 1 (Dockerfile:114). (8) Optional integrations fail soft, not hard: Turnstile is gated behind TURNSTILE_ENABLED at app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:41 so signup works with no keys; the AI provider, Stripe and Browserbase are all optional in the lib/config/env.ts OptionalSchema and none is read at boot. (9) There is no seeded account and no default password anywhere in the fresh-install path: scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs seeds only default badges, and the first admin is made by hand via SQL per app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:276-284.
impact: None. This records the parts of the self-host surface that are correct so a future audit can spend its time on host-01 through host-08 instead.
recommendation: No action. Keep the .dockerignore `!.env.example` ordering, the service_healthy dependency and the /api/v3/health healthcheck target as they are if any of these files are refactored.

title: AI answer engines cannot reach any of this because Cloudflare AI Crawl Control blocks them at the edge, which is a dashboard toggle and not a code change
description: Recorded so nobody spends a day on it in code. The app does its part: app/robots.ts and app/llms.txt/route.ts exist, lib/config/public-paths.ts explicitly allowlists /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt, /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml for session-less crawlers with a comment explaining that AI crawlers carry no cookie, and components/seo/structured-data.tsx emits SoftwareApplication and FAQPage JSON-LD on the landing page including both extension store URLs. None of that reaches an AI crawler, because Cloudflare's Managed robots.txt / AI Crawl Control feature overrides the application's own robots.txt at the edge and disallows GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot and Google-Extended. This was confirmed in prior work as the reason AI assistants do not know the product exists. It is fixed by turning the feature off in the Cloudflare dashboard. Related and separately filed: AUDIT-012#fe-01 found the root layout's await headers() forces all 311 routes dynamic so Cloudflare caches no HTML, which affects crawl budget for the roughly 780 SEO pages, and AUDIT-013#subdeps-01 found the npm name vulnradar is unclaimed while /docs/cli advertises npx vulnradar.
impact: None directly. It explains why the marketing surface described in the other findings does not appear in AI answers, and it prevents a future auditor from proposing code fixes for an edge configuration problem.
recommendation: No code change. The owner toggles Managed robots.txt / AI Crawl Control off in the Cloudflare dashboard for vulnradar.dev. Once that is done, the llms.txt and JSON-LD work already in the repo starts being read, and mkt-07's APP_DESCRIPTION rewrite becomes the sentence AI answers actually quote, which is a reason to do mkt-07 before or alongside the toggle.

title: Route-level loading and error boundaries are missing on 61 of 71 pages, but almost every gap is already covered by an in-page state ladder, so the real exposure is narrower than the raw count suggests
description: Measured for this audit, extending AUDIT-011#drift-13 rather than re-filing it. loading.tsx exists for /admin, /assets, /compare, /dashboard, /history, /pricing, /profile, /repos, /shares, /teams (10). error.tsx exists for the same set minus /pricing and /repos (8, plus app/error.tsx and app/global-error.tsx). not-found.tsx exists once, at the root. Of the 61 pages without a route-level loading.tsx, the ones that actually block on data almost all carry their own in-page gate: /shared/[token] and /host/[hostname] render SharedScanSkeleton (app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:137, app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:135), /public-scans renders PublicScansTableSkeleton (:134), /badge renders BadgeSkeleton (:88), /browser/[id] gates at :519, all three /checkout/* pages render CheckoutSkeleton (for example app/checkout/credits/page.tsx:65-67), and /dashboard wraps its own content in Suspense with a real skeleton fallback (app/dashboard/page.tsx:169). The 17 pages that are async server components (all of /legal, /tools, /alternatives, /checks, /security, /landing) resolve from the local registry and config rather than the database, so a missing loading.tsx there costs a paint, not a hang. The genuinely uncovered blocking surfaces are the ones filed separately above and in AUDIT-011#auth-08 (/login, /signup, /reset-password prerender `Suspense fallback={null}`) and #ck-06 (/contact's ticket list returns null while loading). Recorded so the next audit does not re-derive the 61-page number as if it were 61 blank screens.
impact: None directly. This is a negative result: the loading.tsx count understates the product's actual coverage, and prioritising by that count alone would spend effort on static pages while the real blank-screen and never-resolving cases (state-04, state-06, state-08) sit elsewhere.
recommendation: When acting on AUDIT-011#drift-13, prioritise error.tsx over loading.tsx: the segments that most need a boundary are /host/[hostname], /shared/[token] and /browser/[id], where a render-time throw on untrusted server data currently escapes to the full-screen app/error.tsx and destroys the public page chrome. loading.tsx can be skipped entirely for the 17 async server pages.

title: There are no actionable TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX markers and no commented-out code blocks anywhere in the source: all 14 marker matches are scanner detection patterns or display placeholders
category: verified clean: deferred-work markers and commented-out code
description: Item 6 of the scope expected 14 TODO-family markers across app, lib, components, extension/src, cli and scripts. All 14 matches exist, and none is a deferred-work marker. Seven are the scanner's own detection logic, which looks for these strings in the sites it scans: lib/scanner/checks/content.ts:841 (comment naming the keyword set), :1899 (the regex /(?:TODO|FIXME|XXX|HACK|console\.log|debugger)/i) and :1902 (its finding message); lib/scanner/checks/information-disclosure.ts:456-457 (a comment recording that this keyword family was deliberately REMOVED from that check because it fires on nearly every real site); lib/scanner/checks/vibe-code.ts:91 and :93 (a regex for a TODO comment naming an unimplemented security control, and its message). The other seven are the literal string 'XXXX' used as a formatting placeholder or a fake key: lib/scanner/checks/content.ts:1641, lib/scanner/checks/secrets-extended.ts:24, lib/ai/verify-context.ts:93, app/api/v3/auth/me/route.ts:122, app/api/v3/auth/2fa/setup/route.ts:31, app/api/v3/auth/2fa/backup-codes/route.ts:18 and components/auth/login-2fa-form.tsx:143 (the backup-code input placeholder 'XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX'). Nothing in extension/src, cli/ or scripts/ matches at all. Separately, item 5: I scanned every .ts/.tsx/.mjs file outside node_modules for runs of three or more consecutive // lines whose content parses as code, and then for any single line matching ^\s*//\s*(const|let|var|import|export|return|await|function|class|if \(|for \(|console\.log). Both produced only prose. There is no commented-out code in this repository.
impact: None: this is a clean result. It is recorded so a later audit does not spend the same effort re-deriving it, and so the 14 raw grep hits are not mistaken for a backlog. The one thing worth knowing is that a real TODO added to this codebase today would be the only one, so a lint rule that forbids them would pass immediately.
recommendation: No action required. If the owner wants to keep it that way, add 'no-warning-comments' at warn level for terms TODO/FIXME/HACK to eslint.config.mjs, scoped to app/, lib/, components/ and hooks/, and exclude lib/scanner/checks/ where those strings are detection data rather than notes.

title: npm audit is clean, every package resolves from the public registry, and the lockfile's Linux native bindings are intact
description: Recording the negative results so the next audit does not redo them. `npm audit --json` on the full tree reports 0 vulnerabilities across 813 packages (369 prod, 363 dev, 137 optional, 1 peer) at every severity including info, so there is no reachability analysis to do: nothing is reported. `npm view <pkg> deprecated` across all 86 direct dependencies returns nothing, and no lockfile entry carries a `deprecated` field. Scanning all 814 lockfile entries, every single `resolved` URL points at https://registry.npmjs.org: there are no git URLs, no tarball URLs, no alternate registries and no `file:` links. Exactly three entries have `hasInstallScript: true` (core-js 3.49.0, fsevents 2.3.3 which is macOS-only and optional, and unrs-resolver 1.12.2 which is dev-only), and Dockerfile:24 runs with `--ignore-scripts` anyway (see deps-05). Most importantly given this repo's history: the committed lockfile still contains the full set of Linux native bindings that a Windows regeneration strips. Verified present: @next/swc-linux-x64-gnu, -x64-musl, -arm64-gnu and -arm64-musl all at 15.5.23; @img/sharp-linux-x64, @img/sharp-linuxmusl-x64 and @img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64; @tailwindcss/oxide-linux-x64-gnu and -musl at 4.3.3; @unrs/resolver-binding-linux-x64-gnu and -musl at 1.12.2; lightningcss-linux-x64-gnu and -musl at both 1.33.0 and 1.32.0. package-lock.json is tracked by git and .gitignore has no lock entry. The Node version story is consistent everywhere it is stated: .nvmrc `22`, .node-version `22`, all five ci.yml jobs `node-version: "22"`, Dockerfile:11 and :62 node:22.11.0-alpine, package.json:8 `>=22.0.0` (see deps-07 on tightening that upper bound).
impact: No action required. Two things here are worth an operator knowing: the lockfile is currently healthy on the exact axis that has broken this repo before, so whoever applies deps-01, deps-02 or deps-08 needs to regenerate it on Linux or graft entries by hand rather than running npm install on Windows; and `npm audit` being clean means the CI gate at ci.yml (`npm audit --audit-level=high --omit=dev`) is currently passing on merit rather than on a suppression.
recommendation: No change. When applying any of the package.json edits in this section, re-run the Linux-binding check afterwards: the thirteen entries listed above must still be present in package-lock.json before the change is committed.

title: SQL, XSS, path-traversal, command-injection, deserialization and secret-exposure surfaces were swept clean this pass, so the next audit can skip re-deriving them
category: injection surfaces verified clean (scope note, no action required)
description:
Recorded so this ground is not re-walked. SQL: every pool.query interpolation site was opened. The only dynamic SQL fragments are whitelist-derived (app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts:210-230 filters against an ALLOWED_COLUMNS Set; lib/auth/authorization.ts:292 derives both table and owner column from the OWNERSHIP map; app/api/v3/history/[id]/route.ts:339-357 and app/api/v3/schedules/route.ts:301-315 build SET clauses from server-side literals only; app/api/v3/ai/conversations/route.ts:155-178 and app/api/v3/admin/support-tickets/route.ts:35-45 build WHERE from validated enums). No dynamic ORDER BY, no `IN (${...})` list building, no string-concatenated table names. lib/domains/scope.ts:50 uses a DB value as a LIKE right-hand side, but lib/domains/verification.ts:45 constrains it to `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$`.

XSS: only three dangerouslySetInnerHTML sites exist outside the scanner's own detection strings (components/ui/chart.tsx:82 config-derived, app/layout.tsx:158 a nonce'd bootstrap over JSON.stringify'd constants, components/seo/structured-data.tsx:57 through safeJsonLd's `<`/`>`/`&` escape). No innerHTML anywhere in extension/src. Every notification/scan-result href sink goes through safeHref (lib/ui/utils.ts:19). Emails escape scan data (lib/email/email.ts:1305, :1375, :1462, :1538). Markdown/compliance exports escape via lib/reports/md-escape.ts; the PDF writer escapes `\`, `(`, `)` at lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:51; SARIF is JSON.stringify.

Path traversal: avatars are BYTEA rows, not files (lib/uploads/avatar-storage.ts), and the upload path enforces a PNG/JPEG MIME plus magic-bytes allowlist (app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts:255-290). app/api/v3/ai/context/route.ts:18-25 joins only fixed literal segments. app/api/v3/admin/backup/route.ts has no download-by-name. The updater extracts with `tar -xzf -C <tmp>` after checksum and cosign verification (lib/updater/apply.ts:178-189).

Command injection: the only child_process users are lib/updater/exec.ts, lib/backup/run-backup.ts and scripts/, all argv arrays with `shell: false`. No eval, new Function, vm, or request-derived dynamic import anywhere in app/, lib/, components/ or extension/src.

Prototype pollution: no recursive merge helper exists; the one `{...updates}` spread of a request body (app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts:203) is filtered through an allowlist Set immediately after.

Secrets: no hardcoded credentials outside scanner test fixtures and docs placeholders; the only NEXT_PUBLIC_ vars hold an app URL, a Turnstile site key, a Stripe publishable key and SEO verification tokens; no token/secret/password value is passed to console.*; no route returns a secret column (lib/history/resolve-scan.ts:61 does `SELECT *` but every caller projects explicit fields).
impact: None. This is a coverage record.
recommendation: No action. If a future change adds a dynamic ORDER BY, a raw-HTML markdown renderer, a filesystem-backed upload path, or a recursive config merge, re-open the corresponding item above.
